description:
40 Lammas Green is ground floor flat on the end in 1950’s listed block. I have owned it since 2008; the flat is currently tenanted. The freeholder is the City of London.
The property suffers from poor ventilation and is subject to black mould and mildew. I was therefore concerned about the health risks to the tenants so I commissioned a damp survey from a reputable company Dampworks Ltd. 
Their findings indicate:
The relative humidity within the property regularly exceeds 70%, and ideally should be 45%. 
Despite supplying dehumidifiers, because the property is on the ground floor there is limited through ventilation. 
There is no mechanical ventilation in the bathroom and the property doesn’t reach the minimum standards for extraction.
The report and visual inspection show that there is a condensation problem with the associated black mould growth and risk to health.

Damp works recommended the following remedial actions:
Install a positive pressure flat unit - input ventilation system flat-tec pro (the smallest on the market) for improved ventilation. This unit is fitted inside the property on an external wall and brings fresh dry air into the property at low pressure. The humid damp air is then forced from the property at low pressure. The unit will remain running when the property is unoccupied negating the need to leave windows open and associated security unit. 
Install a baffled passive vent for cross-flow ventilation. This unit will allow fresh air into the property and has been carefully chosen for its ultra small size. The cross section measures 200mmx200mm to ensure minimum impact on the historic property whilst dealing with 21st living and health and safety requirements.
Together with applying a mould sterilisation fluid to the affected areas.

Both the positive pressure unit and baffled vent would require a core drill through the external wall at the side of the building and have small discrete external brown grills on them. This is the SW elevation and faces a small car park. I have spoken to the City of London and they require permission from Lewisham Council before agreeing to the works.
It’s worth pointing out that many of the other flats in the block have small grills on them, often coming out of the bathroom and on the front of the property
